Remove weak edges from a heterogeneous transition network

Source: R/prune_htna.R
prune_htna.Rd

prune_htna() removes weak edges from a heterogeneous transition network so that the plot and the descriptive measures focus on the transitions that carry the process. A relative transition network estimated from many sessions is usually dense: almost every code is followed by almost every other code at least once, and most of these transitions are rare. Because the weights are kept in the network and only set aside, pruning can be undone or re-applied.

prune_htna() sets to zero the edges that fail a rule: weights below a fixed threshold (method = "threshold", the default), the lowest share of the weights (method = "lowest"), or edges that are not supported by a bootstrap (method = "bootstrap", with boot from bootstrap_htna()). It runs Nestimate's net_prune() with the actor partition kept, so plot_htna() and the other functions work on the pruned network unchanged. It returns an htna network with the removed edges set to zero and the rule recorded.

deprune_htna() restores the removed edges, reprune_htna() removes them again, and pruning_details_htna() lists them.

Usage

prune_htna(x, ...)

Arguments

x

An htna network from build_htna().

...

Pruning rule: method ("threshold", default, "lowest" or "bootstrap"), threshold (default 0.1), lowest (default 0.05), level (default 0.5) and boot (a bootstrap result for method = "bootstrap").

Value

An htna network of the same class and structure as build_htna() returns, with the removed edges set to zero in its weight matrix and the rule recorded for deprune_htna(), reprune_htna() and pruning_details_htna().

See also

deprune_htna(), reprune_htna(), pruning_details_htna(), bootstrap_htna().

Examples

data(human_ai)
net <- build_htna(human_ai, actor_type = "actor_type")
#> Metadata aggregated per session: ties resolved by first occurrence in 'session_date' (1 sessions), 'cluster' (42 sessions), 'actor_type' (24 sessions)
pruned <- prune_htna(net, threshold = 0.05)
summary(pruned)
